findings.category: availability / unauthenticated memory pinning (challenges A36-007 'idle socket lives about 83 s')
findings.evidence: Default server (app.ts createServer without options: headersTimeout 60 s, requestTimeout 300 s, maxConnections undefined, no per-IP cap; readJson buffers up to 64 KiB per request). Real `node src/server.ts` on :3814: 3000 TCP connections each sent a POST /api/auth/login header with Content-Length: 65000 plus 60,000 body bytes and then stopped. RSS 100 MB -> 328 MB (about 76 KB held per socket; 1-byte-body sockets cost 14 KB: 5000 sockets 99 -> 169 MB). /api/health stayed fast (p95 3 ms), so nobody is stalled, but the memory is pinned for the whole request timeout. Close times measured on single sockets: idle or partial headers 90 s (408), partial body 330 s (408), keep-alive after a request 6 s. 3000 sockets cost the attacker 180 MB of upload once; 13,000 sockets from one host pin about 1 GB, 20,000 about 1.5 GB for 5.5 minutes, repeatable. No authentication, no account, works in default and DEMO mode; also bypasses every rate limit because limits are applied only after the body is read. A36-007 only documents idle sockets of about 83 s and a P3 rating.
findings.fix_hint: Reject an oversized declared Content-Length (>64 KiB) on the headers before reading anything; set server.requestTimeout to ~15-30 s and headersTimeout ~10 s (JSON bodies are tiny); set server.maxConnections or cap per IP at the reverse proxy; document the proxy requirement in README.

findings.category: scale / class size has no cap (teacher analytics 500 and multi-second blocking)
findings.evidence: Class analytics cost per call, real process, class of N students with 9 completed attempts each (direct SQL fixtures): N=2,500 583 ms; 5,000 1,313 ms; 10,000 3,018 ms; 20,000 6,777 ms with RSS 118 MB -> 756 MB (cost per student rises 0.23 -> 0.34 ms, so slightly worse than linear). Roster at 100,001 members: 1,363 ms and 27.7 MB. HARD FAILURE: GET /api/classes/:id/analytics answers 500 {"error":{"code":"internal_error"}} as soon as a class has 32,767 members (server log: `Error: too many SQL variables`, game.ts analytics() builds `user_id IN (?,?,...)` from every member id); 32,766 members still answers 200 in 844 ms. Roster endpoint keeps working. Cost for the attacker: one account per member (registration is 100/hour/IP by default, unbounded behind an IPv6 /64, A36-002) and the join code of the target class; joinClass has no capacity limit.
findings.fix_hint: Cap class size (for example 500) in joinClass or paginate; chunk the IN list or use a temp table / join on class_members instead of binding every id; build the analytics per-mission aggregates in SQL instead of 5 x bestRows per student.

findings.category: availability / reads take the write lock (busy_timeout blocks the whole event loop)
findings.evidence: Game.badges() (game.ts:268-269) runs tx(this.db, ...) = BEGIN IMMEDIATE on every GET /api/badges, /api/dashboard and /api/profile even when nothing is granted. With a second process holding the write lock for 3 s (BEGIN IMMEDIATE on the same DB file, which README/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS say is a supported 'two processes' setup), `GET /api/badges` answered 200 after 2,996 ms and a concurrent unrelated `GET /api/health` also took 2,996 ms (node:sqlite busy handler sleeps synchronously inside the event loop; busy_timeout=5000, so a 5 s holder turns these GETs into 500). Single process: not reachable. HEAD requests skip it (readOnlyRequest).
findings.fix_hint: Skip the write transaction when SELECT shows nothing to grant (check conditions first, BEGIN IMMEDIATE only if a badge is missing), or move the catch-up out of the read path; state the single-writer assumption.

findings.category: availability / successful logins are not throttled (scrypt thread pool)
findings.evidence: routes.ts login gives its failure slots back on success, so correct-password logins are unlimited. One IP, 8 own accounts x 7 in-flight loops (56 in flight, below the 60 per-IP and 8 per-account in-flight reservations): victim login latency 36 ms idle -> 448-464 ms (5 samples), flood throughput 773 logins in 4.5 s; with a single account the 8-slot reservation caps it (victim 66-92 ms). /api/health and authenticated routes are unaffected (scrypt runs on the 4-thread libuv pool). A non-NFC password doubles the scrypt work per attempt (auth.ts verifyPassword). Several source IPs scale it (not seconds from one IP).
findings.fix_hint: Count successes in a separate generous per-IP/per-account bucket (for example 30 per minute) or bound concurrent scrypt jobs; document UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE.

findings.category: storage growth / attacker-controlled bytes in answer_log
findings.evidence: game.ts:405 stores safeJson(response).slice(0, 2000) for every answered step; `response` is only schema-checked as an object, extra keys are ignored by checkResponse. Real server: 100 wrong answers {"stepId":"hem-01-s1","response":{"pad":"x"*60000,"x":0,"y":0}} -> 100 x 200 OK, answer_log AVG(length(response_json)) = 2000, 200,000 bytes. At the default 120 answers/min that is 240 KB/min = 14.4 MB/hour = 345 MB/day per account (the cap of 400 rows applies per attempt only, new attempts are unlimited), about 20x the normal row size. Not read by any request path (streak/lastActive read only created_at).
findings.fix_hint: Store a normalised response (only the engine's expected fields, or the hash/length), or cap total answer_log rows per user.

findings.category: scale / default leaderboard is O(all users)
findings.evidence: game.ts:878 loads `SELECT id, name FROM users` for every leaderboard call, including the default cohort=class. 100,000 student rows (class of 38): GET /api/leaderboard 86 / 71 / 70 ms, 20 concurrent -> /api/health p50 54 ms, max 208 ms. cohort=all (A37-002, known): 1,558 ms per call and 20 concurrent calls -> health p50 1,539 ms at 100k users (about 15 us per user). Linear, as documented; the default path was documented as cheap.
findings.fix_hint: Query names only for the ids returned (WHERE id IN) or join once; cache the all-cohort ranking for a few seconds.

findings.category: availability / demo reset is unthrottled and linear in history (DEMO_MODE only)
findings.evidence: POST /api/demo/reset (routes.ts:255) has no limiter. Fresh seed: 8-12 ms (student), 3 ms (teacher); flood from one token 199/s (1 loop), 306/s (5), 323/s (20 loops) with /api/health p50 54 ms at 20 loops. Cost grows with what the shared Alex account accumulated (DELETE cascade + replay in one transaction): 5,000 attempts 108 ms, 50,000 attempts 1,208 ms (health 1,202 ms during it), i.e. about 14 hours of default-limit play. Linear, DEMO_MODE only, and the reset itself wipes the history.
findings.fix_hint: Add limiter.hit('reset:'+uid, 6, 60_000); optionally cap attempts per account.
